intro: Indiana runs its elections county by county, through each county's circuit court clerk and county election board, with the Secretary of State's Election Division overseeing the state.

id_rule.text: Bring a government-issued photo ID to the polls. It must show your name and photo, and it must be an Indiana or U.S. government ID that is not expired or expired after the last general election.

src.label: Indiana Secretary of State — photo ID law

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: The deadline is the close of business at your county voter registration office, or midnight if you register online.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote early in person at the circuit court clerk's office or a satellite site until noon on Monday, Nov. 2. The clerk's office must be open for at least seven hours on Saturdays, Oct. 24 and Oct. 31.

src.label: Indiana Secretary of State — absentee voting

dates.label: Mail ballot application must be received
dates.detail: Your county must have your application by 11:59 pm. Indiana allows only certain voters to vote by mail, for example voters age 65 or older.

src.label: Indiana Secretary of State — absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6 am to 6 pm, local time. A mail ballot must be received by your county election board by 6 pm. A postmark does not count.

src.label: Indiana Secretary of State — absentee voting
